text: I was raised in the temple.
Most of my life has been spent maintaining traditions.
Many traditions have no recorded explanation.
People often become uncomfortable when asked why a ritual exists.
The Song has been preserved for generations.
Nobody alive understands its language.
I have copied the Song many times.
Several old versions differ slightly.
The differences are usually ignored.
I do not think they should be.
Nara experienced dreams near the palace-monument complex when she was younger.
She rarely discusses them.
I have never experienced such dreams.
The small ancient shrine contains symbols similar to those found on temple artifacts.
No one has translated them.
Renu believes the symbols form a written language.
I think he may be correct.
The Agnikanda remains poorly documented.
Temple records from that period are incomplete.
Several pages appear to be missing.
Nobody knows where they went.
Older villagers avoid discussing those missing records.
The palace-monument complex contains sealed areas.
Temple tradition forbids entering them.
The reason for the prohibition was never recorded.
Chapala asks questions most people avoid.
He reminds me of certain stories about the founders.
Ila's husband spent time studying old records before he disappeared.
He borrowed several documents from the temple.
Those documents were never returned.
